body.heading: Where in the world is United States?
paragraphs: United States is a country in Northern America, which is part of North America.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of United States is Washington D.C.. Washington, D.C. is the capital — the 'D.C.' stands for District of Columbia, a special district that belongs to no single state.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: The language you will hear most in United States is English.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of United States is the US dollar.

body.heading: How big is United States?
paragraphs: United States covers about 9,629,000 square kilometres of land and inland water.

body.heading: A fact to wow your friends
paragraphs: Yellowstone National Park contains geysers heated by geothermal energy. Old Faithful is Yellowstone's most famous geyser, erupting on a schedule rangers can predict. Under the park sleeps a giant volcano — a supervolcano.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: The Grand Canyon is a mile deep and 18 miles wide — families ride the rim train, walk the Trail of Time and watch the rocks change colour at sunset.
Yellowstone, the world's first national park, has geysers like Old Faithful, rainbow hot springs and valleys of bison, elk and bears.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find United States on a map or globe. Which continent is it on — and can you name a country that sits next to it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?
